item.title: Sweden’s Far-Right Leader Seeks a Comeback as Election Nears
item.description: Swedish far-right leader Jimmie Akesson kicked off the final two weeks of a tight election campaign with a speech in his home town aimed rallying supporters and closing a consistent polling gap.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Duxbury

item.title: Niger Rulers Say Army Mutiny Contained After Gunfire in Capital
item.description: Niger said it contained a mutiny by soldiers who detained some of their colleagues at a military base and fired on sites in the capital, the first major challenge from within the armed forces to the junta that seized power three years ago.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Olurounbi

item.title: US Canada Trade Fight Shows Few Signs of Easing
item.description: The US and Canada appear to be headed for a prolonged trade standoff, with no current negotiations and Canadian officials expecting serious talks may not resume until after the US midterm elections. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason and Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet are on Bloomberg This Weekend with Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz to discuss the economic pain on both sides of the border, Canada’s push to diversify its trade and whether Prime Minister Mark Carney’s resistance to President Donald Trump could influence how other US allies respond. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Keeps Building His Ballroom Amid Supreme Court’s Silence
item.description: Construction on President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom shows no signs of slowing down. And the US Supreme Court shows no signs of wanting to stop it.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Trump Backlash Adds New Risks to the Stocks the Government Owns
item.description: Traders have made a bundle over the past year following President Donald Trump as the US government pursues an unprecedented strategy of taking ownership stakes in publicly traded companies.
item.dc:creator: Norah Rami and Matthew Griffin

item.title: Republicans See Trump’s Unceasing Iran War as Midterm Threat
item.description: Six months into a conflict that President Donald Trump predicted would last “four to five weeks,” Republican strategists worry there’s no way to keep the Iran war from hurting the party’s prospects in November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Green and Nancy Cook

item.title: Ukraine Says Russia Planning Ground Offensive on Kyiv, Chernihiv
item.description: Ukraine has received intelligence that Russia is preparing for a possible new ground offensive toward Kyiv as well as Chernihiv in the nation’s far north, a top official said.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova

item.title: Death Toll at 37 From Russian Strike on Warehouse Near Kyiv
item.description: At least 37 people were killed in a village west of Kyiv when a warehouse detonated following a Russian drone strike, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy vowed an investigation into why explosives had been stored in a densely populated area.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova and Ros Krasny

item.title: Iceland Heads to Polls in Tight Referendum on EU Entry Talks
item.description: Icelanders began voting on Saturday on whether to reopen membership talks with the European Union in a referendum that’s testing the bloc’s geopolitical appeal.
item.dc:creator: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir and Ott Ummelas

item.title: Russia Is Teaching Its Children to Fight the Wars of the Future
item.description: Students returning to Russian schools next week will discover a change to their civics courses that puts military training at the heart of the lessons.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Reform UK Seeks to Play Down Crypto, Show Off Diplomatic Clout
item.description: Reform UK is highlighting its diplomatic clout and de-emphasizing support from crypto companies as Nigel Farage’s populist party seeks to show that it’s ready to lead Britain.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: ICE Explores Purchasing Robot Dogs in Enforcement Tech Push
item.description: The Trump administration is exploring adding robot dogs to the expanding arsenal being used by federal immigration authorities as they seek to boost arrests and deportations across the country.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Trump Teleprompter Pays $170,000 to End Insider Trading Probe
item.description: A White House teleprompter operator will pay more than $172,000 to end a federal regulator’s probe into alleged well-timed prediction market bets about President Donald Trump’s speeches.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Nepal Seeks Foreign Help as Scale of Flood Disaster Grows
item.description: Nepal sought international help to cope with the aftermath of catastrophic flash floods that have left nearly 3,000 people missing along the mountainous border with China.
item.dc:creator: Dan Strumpf, Kanupriya Kapoor and Akriti Sharma

item.title: US War With Iran Hits Six Month Mark | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/28/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments on interest rates were the “least interesting” part of his Jackson Hole speech and points instead to his focus on the availability of credit. Democratic Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts discusses her bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which aims to create federal oversight of the most advanced AI models through reporting, independent audits, and emergency safeguards. Sec. Leon Panetta, former US Secretary of Defense, says the US is “now trapped in another forever war” with Iran after six months of fighting with “no end in sight.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sec. Panetta: US Is Trapped In Another Forever War
item.description: Sec. Leon Panetta, former US Secretary of Defense, says the US is “now trapped in another forever war” with Iran after six months of fighting with “no end in sight.” Panetta says Iran is essentially holding the US economy hostage through its control of the Strait of Hormuz and argues President Trump needs to find a way to open the critical waterway. He says US efforts to clear mines have not taken away Iran’s leverage as Tehran continues to threaten ships and use missiles to restrict traffic through the strait. Panetta says there is “no way to take control of this war” as long as Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Trahan: Federal AI Governance Is 'Missing'
item.description: Democratic Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts discusses her bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which aims to create federal oversight of the most advanced AI models through reporting, independent audits and emergency safeguards.. Rep. Trahan calls criticism that the bill would broadly preempt state laws "completely false," arguing instead it creates a "narrow federal lane" while preserving state authority in areas including privacy and consumer protection. She also calls for hearings with leading AI companies and broader bipartisan action on data centers, workers, and AI in schools. She speaks with Tyler Kendall and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US to Take Control of Major Portion of Venezuelan Oil Wealth
item.description: The US is set to take majority control over a huge amount of Venezuela’s oil wealth in an unprecedented maneuver that officials said would create the world’s second-largest private oil company by reserves and secure American petroleum supplies for decades to come.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Eric Martin

item.title: Duppler: Warsh’s Credit Message Mattered More Than Rates
item.description: Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments on interest rates were the “least interesting” part of his Jackson Hole speech and points instead to his focus on the availability of credit. Duppler says Warsh offered confidence to markets about credit and liquidity, arguing that message takes on added importance as federal debt tops $40 trillion and the AI buildout creates significant capital needs. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ICE Deports Right-Wing Provocateur, Influencer Milo Yiannopoulos
item.description: Federal immigration authorities said they deported right-wing provocateur and online influencer Milo Yiannopoulos after he was detained and accused of overstaying his visa.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell
